tier_reason: A stands; the suite's allocator asymmetry works against cppcoro, so its fork-join wins hold.

corrections.caveats: Enricher: the measured code is the andreasbuhr/cppcoro fork (active through 2026-06-12), which differs from upstream: its static_thread_pool counts sleepers once (notify_intent_to_sleep uses exchange) and it adds a Linux epoll io_service and sockets, so upstream cannot run io_socket_st on Linux. Symmetric transfer is enabled only on Clang 7+ (GCC and MSVC fall back to an atomic handshake, issue #216); the local-queue cap check (m_mask == max_local_queue_size) is unreachable, so the 1 MB cap never applies. Open issues #209 (tsan race in sync_wait) and #221 (cancellation deadlock).

tier_reason: A to C: the only like-for-like win (io_socket_st, 9%, one run) comes from an asymmetric harness: cppcoro's timer includes io_service stop() and two thread joins while libcoro's stops before scheduler teardown, and libcoro links tcmalloc while cppcoro does not; the channel row is cross-config. Asymmetric-baseline downgrade precedent.

corrections.caveats: Enricher: in io_socket_st, cppcoro's timed region includes io_service stop() plus two thread joins while libcoro's ends before scheduler teardown, and libcoro gets tcmalloc against cppcoro's non-tcmalloc allocator; with one run and a 9% margin (41643 us) the win is unproven. The suite pins 44d12235 (PR #433), before the io_scheduler-to-scheduler rename (#435), the Read/Write API (#436) and the scheduler lock removal (#444). thread_pool is a single mutex-guarded FIFO deque at the pin and at HEAD although the README says work stealing; FIFO gives breadth-first fork-join and the 14.66 GB RSS (issues #404 and #446 open, Chase-Lev PR #450 unmerged).
